questions.stem: In fog you hear a vessel's horn sounding continuously, with no pattern and no breaks. What is the most likely meaning?
options: A power-driven vessel making way
A distress signal: continuous sounding with fog-signalling apparatus
A vessel at anchor
A vessel overtaking in a narrow channel
questions.explanation: A continuous sounding with any fog-signalling apparatus is an Annex IV distress signal. A power-driven vessel making way sounds one prolonged blast at intervals, an anchored vessel rings a bell, and overtaking signals are a set pattern of prolonged and short blasts.

questions.stem: Which of these is a distress signal under Annex IV?
options: A white hand flare
A green star rocket
A smoke signal giving off orange smoke
A yellow flashing light
questions.explanation: Orange smoke is listed in Annex IV. The listed pyrotechnics are red: red stars, red parachute flares and red hand flares. White flares, green stars and yellow flashing lights are not distress signals.

questions.stem: Which sound signal is listed in Annex IV as a distress signal?
options: Five short and rapid blasts
One prolonged blast every 2 minutes
Four short blasts
A gun or other explosive signal fired at intervals of about a minute
questions.explanation: A gun or other explosive signal fired at about one-minute intervals is an Annex IV distress signal, as is a continuous fog signal. Five short is the Rule 34 doubt signal, one prolonged every 2 minutes is a power-driven vessel making way in fog, and four short is the pilot vessel identity signal.

questions.stem: A drifting fishing boat is flying a square flag with a round fender hung just above it. What should you take this to mean?
options: She is in distress and needs assistance
She is fishing with gear extended
She is at anchor
She is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
questions.explanation: A square flag with a ball, or anything resembling a ball, above or below it is an Annex IV distress signal. Improvised versions count; a fender can stand in for the ball. A single ball alone is the anchor shape, and the fishing and restricted-in-ability shapes are different.

questions.stem: Which group lists only Annex IV radio or electronic distress signals?
options: VHF channel 16 routine call, AIS position report, radar echo
MAYDAY by radiotelephone, DSC distress alert on VHF channel 70, EPIRB signals
SECURITE call, weather broadcast, DSC routine call
PAN-PAN call, VHF channel 13 bridge-to-bridge call, navigation warning
questions.explanation: MAYDAY by radiotelephone, a DSC distress alert (VHF channel 70 or MF/HF), satellite distress alerts, EPIRB signals and approved signals such as survival craft radar transponders are all listed. PAN-PAN is an urgency signal and SECURITE a safety signal; routine calls and position reports are not distress signals.

questions.stem: Which flag signal from the International Code means distress?
options: A alone
C over N
N over C
O alone
questions.explanation: The International Code signal of distress is N over C (NC). Reversing the order does not give the same signal. Single flags A and O have other meanings in the International Code of Signals.

questions.stem: Annex IV mentions two aids that help aircraft identify a vessel in distress. What are they?
options: A white sheet and a mirror
A red flag and a smoke float
Navigation lights left on in daylight and a radar reflector
Orange canvas with a black square and circle (or other suitable symbol), and a dye marker
questions.explanation: Annex IV draws attention to a piece of orange canvas with a black square and circle (or other suitable symbol) for identification from the air, and a dye marker. The other combinations may help in practice but are not the items named.

questions.stem: At night in Canadian waters you see a high-intensity white light flashing steadily at about one flash per second from a low position on the water. How should you treat it?
options: As a possible distress signal, since a white light flashing 50 to 70 times a minute is reported as a Canadian distress signal
As an aid to navigation, so check the chart and carry on
As a vessel at anchor
As a fishing vessel hauling nets
questions.explanation: A secondary source reports that the Canadian Annex IV lists a high-intensity white light flashing at regular intervals of 50 to 70 times a minute (about one per second) as a distress signal in Canadian waters. Treat it as possible distress: note the bearing and time and tell the master. Anchor lights are steady, not flashing. This Canadian item still needs confirming against the current text.
